contrary_evidence: WHO TrACSS 2026 reports 173 of 183 countries with plans, while only 22% report both funding and full implementation and 36% report reference-laboratory capacity.
WOAH ANIMUSE 2024 covers 74% of estimated global food-producing animal biomass with 119 participants; 83,254 tonnes were reported and the coverage-adjusted estimate is 86,346 tonnes.
Only five of 119 quantitative ANIMUSE participants selected farm records as a validated quantitative source; most data came from sales and imports.

The 80-participant ANIMUSE cohort shows a 3% decline from 2019 to 2024, while a distinct 74-participant analysis is cited as showing a 9% increase from 2018 to 2024; the cohorts and periods must remain separate.
ECDC 2025 data show at least 50% third-generation cephalosporin resistance in K. pneumoniae in 21 of 43 reporting countries and at least 50% carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter spp. in 21 of 38.
The EU incidence of carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae bloodstream infection was 3.75 per 100,000 in 2025, 72% above 2019 and 1.68 above the EU 2030 target of 2.07.
The 2024 UN declaration commits to meaningful reduction of antimicrobials used globally in agrifood systems by 2030.
limitations: TrACSS is a national self-assessment, not an independent audit of budget execution or service quality.
ANIMUSE quantities are primarily derived from sales/import records; only five of 119 quantitative participants used farm records.
The ANIMUSE 2019–2024 and 2018–2024 trends use different participant cohorts and periods.
ECDC country-threshold results concern invasive clinical isolates, not community prevalence.
The EU-level ESAC-Net targets and population-weighted indicators must be distinguished from the separate EU/EEA community-consumption series.
The available datasets do not establish a causal link between animal antimicrobial use and the human resistance patterns presented.
